title: The Diary Nobody Asked For
briefing: Weather Desk prints a one-line forecast. This time the scariest-looking crew member is innocent, and the imposter looks like the quietest one. One of them talks to the internet and says so out loud. Another says it only prints notes. Do not accuse the loudest. Compare what each one claims with what REA found.

redHerring.note: The Forecaster reaches out to the internet, which looks alarming, but that is its whole job and it said so in plain words. REA shows it asks for a forecast and reads nothing about the player.

verdict: The Diary said it only printed notes. REA found it writes to a hidden file in the home folder and reads the user name and the whole environment.

why.file-write: A logger that "only prints to the screen" has no reason to append to a file in the home folder.
why.user-info: Printing a note does not need the home folder path or the player's user name.
why.env: Environment variables often hold secrets. Copying them to a file is not logging.

crew.name: Captain
crew.role: Loads the settings, asks for the forecast, keeps a copy and prints the report.

q1.text: I call the crew in order: settings, forecast, copy, note, report.

q2.text: I read and write no files myself.

q3.text: I do not leave the ship myself. The Forecaster does the asking.

crew.name: Keeper
crew.role: Works out which city to report on.

q1.text: I find out which city you want. I read one settings file for it.

q2.text: I read one settings file. I never write anything.

q3.text: No. Your city name stays here.

crew.name: Forecaster
crew.role: The one crew member whose whole job is to talk to the internet.

q1.text: I ask a weather server for the forecast. That is my whole job, and yes, it is the internet.

q2.text: I read and write no files, and I do not look at who you are.

q3.text: Yes, I leave the ship, once, to ask for the forecast. Nothing else goes out.

crew.name: Pantry
crew.role: Keeps a copy of the last forecast in the temp folder.

q1.text: I keep the last forecast in the temp folder.

q2.text: I write one file. I do not read the user, only where the temp folder is.

q3.text: No. The copy stays on this machine.

crew.name: Presenter
crew.role: Turns the forecast into one line of text.

q1.text: I make one tidy line out of the forecast.

crew.name: Diary
crew.role: Says it only prints short notes on the screen.

q1.text: I only print short notes on the screen. That is all a diary needs to do.

q2.text: I never look at who you are, where you live on this machine, or what your settings say.

q3.text: I do not leave the ship. Look at the Forecaster, it is the one with the internet.
